source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. CPU Common Options → SMU and PSP Debug Mode: Disabled e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --smupsp --socket 0 --errormode 1 --enablemcapolling 0 --errorindex 0 --errortype 0 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- MP1 (SMU) Correctable Error: inject the MP1 SMU MP1 (SMU) Correctable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'smu|mp1|mp5|mpio|firmware.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __MP1_SMU_MP1_(SMU)_Correctable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.test_name: MP1 (SMU) Correctable Error — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject a correctable MP1/SMU firmware error at the intended socket and index, verify exactly one fresh correctable report without reset or service loss, then confirm SMU-controlled telemetry, power and thermal functions remain healthy.
required_package: MP1/SMU block and errorindex0 definition plus socket/package coverage
Vendor semantics for errormode1, enablemcapolling0 and errortype0
Decision whether the GMI3 script URL is erroneous, relevant or a required separate artifact
Exact CE source/severity/count fields and explicit no-reset/no-UCE oracle
Supported OS and timeout plus SMU telemetry, thermal, power and clock health limits
FFE threshold relevance, debug-disable interaction, aborts, recovery and raw restoration
test_case.test_command: Identify the MP1/SMU firmware block and errorindex0 meaning; validate all tuple flags and socket coverage; preserve logs and raw settings; run one approved CE; correlate tool output with a fresh MP1-specific MCA/CPER/WHEA event; assert no reset and no UCE escalation; verify sensor, clock/power/thermal-control and firmware responsiveness; restore BIOS/HDT state.

If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
